title: Rook Mobility and Persistent Pressure
subtitle: An active rook, an invading king, and a passed pawn

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter V, §26 The Sudden Attack from a Different Side, Example 57

narration.say: Capablanca plays White against Kupchick at Havana in 1913. White has the open e-file and the move.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Lift the rook to the fourth rank.
exercise.success: 1.Re4. The rook can now change wings.

narration.say: White doubles rooks. Black contests the e-file.
Both kings approach the centre.
White shifts the advanced rook to a4. Black defends a7 with the rook.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Put the rook on a5 to restrict Black’s pawns.

narration.say: White challenges d5. The king approaches, but White pushes it back with check.
White supports c5 with d4. Black advances f5.
White exchanges one pair of rooks.

steps.title: A good plan does not excuse inaccuracies

narration.say: White plays f4 and then king to d2. Capablanca criticises both moves and suggests more active rook play.
Black also misses a defensive chance. White transfers the rook from a5 to the kingside.
White advances a4 and keeps the rook active.
The king heads toward the queenside pawns.
White advances the h-pawn. Black must defend on both sides.

steps.title: Do not relax in a superior position

narration.say: White plays b5. Capablanca criticises this move: rook to g7 was preferable.
White finally brings the rook to g7. Black checks and exchanges queenside pawns.
White advances c6 with check and captures h7.
Capablanca says Black missed a further drawing chance with repeated rook checks. The game continues with rook to e7.
White’s h-pawn is ready to run. Black has just captured the pawn on f4.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Advance the passed h-pawn.

narration.say: The white king advances while the h-pawn reaches the seventh rank.
Black gives checks, but the king keeps finding a route forward.
White gives a rook check before promoting.
White promotes. Black must give up the rook to remove the new queen.
White has emerged with a rook against pawns. This lesson stops here, after the decisive promotion sequence.

steps.title: Keep attention until the end

narration.say: The opening advantage was small: an open file, the move, and greater freedom for the rooks.
Rook transfers and king activity created threats on both wings. The distant h-pawn finally forced the decisive exchange.
Capablanca also records mistakes by both players. A superior position is not permission to stop calculating.

steps.source: Even with a good position, a player, no matter how strong, cannot afford to relax his attention even for one move.
